precepts.text: The Most High is sick of them. He endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath, and they were made to be destroyed by God. God had to endure them parading themselves as though they are the people of God. That made the Lord mad. The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man. When the Lord gets loose from his prophecies — because remember, the Lord gave Esau his time to rule, he said until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. When their time is up, that is when he is free to act. But before that happens he has to allow Esau — and I use the word allow. He has to watch this paramecium, I keep calling it. He has to watch this amoeba. He has to watch this germ move around like he is something great. He is sitting there watching him. He said, I want to step in now, but I cannot do it, because right now I am bound by my word. But when he is free from his prophecies, when the prophecies continue to come to pass like they are, when that number of the Israelites wake up, that is when he is free to do what we are about to read here. He shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies. I have long time holden my peace. You hear what the Lord said. I have long time holden my peace. That is the longsuffering there. I have been still, and refrained myself. Do you know what it is like to refrain yourself? He had to hold himself back. He wants to step in, but he says, I am a man of my word. But I want to get in there and deal with you now. You running around parading yourself like you are my people, like you are my sons, like you are my daughters, and I am watching you take advantage of my real children, and I am mad, but I have got to let the prophecies finish out.
precepts.point: Saying, Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers. So there is no getting out of this. There is no changing. There is nothing that a preacher can do. Nobody could stop what we are about to read here. Surely the Lord said that he will fill Babylon the Great with men. As with caterpillers. What is that talking about? Terrorists. The Most High is going to have this place filled up with terrorists from the other nations that are mad because of what Babylon the Great did to their places. She smote the people in wrath and they are mad. So now they say, since you took our riches, you took our diamonds, you took our gold, you took everything from us, and then you tell us that we have got to come over to Babylon the Great to work — not only are we going to work, but we are working to get inside your system, because we are getting ready to take you down. That is how they are talking with these sleeper cells. That is what is going down. So we do not need to be playing games while all this stuff is happening.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says to Babylon the Great, “thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness”: the measure of her evils has come up to the Lord's nostrils. God said, I am sick of you, I have had enough of you. Isaiah shows the Most High getting loose: “The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies.”

He endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath, and they were made to be destroyed by God. God had to endure them parading themselves as though they are the people of God, and that made the Lord mad. Remember, the Lord gave Esau his time to rule, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. When their time is up, that is when he is free to kick ass. Before that, he has to allow Esau. He has to watch this paramecium, this amoeba, this germ move around like he is something great. He wants to step in now, but he is bound by his word. When the prophecies come to pass like they are, when that number of the Israelites wake up, that is when he is free.

“I have long time holden my peace; I have been still, and refrained myself”. That is the longsuffering. Do you know what it is like to refrain yourself? He had to hold himself back. He is a man of his word, but he wants to get in there and deal with them now: you running around parading yourself like you are my people, like you are my sons and my daughters, and I am watching you take advantage of my real children, and I am mad as hell, but I have got to let the prophecies finish out.

“now will I cry like a travailing woman; I will destroy and devour at once.” That now means he is free. Now he is not bound no more, now that number has come in, because the prophecies have been met. Revelation shows the same now: “the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world”. That great red dragon is Edom, Idumea, cast out of his rulership. He deceived the whole world into thinking a white image is Jesus, that these so-called white people are the Jews and the Christians, and that we, the jewels of God, are nothing. Then: “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ”, because Esau is brought down, the times of the nations are fulfilled, and we are ready to rule.

So when Jeremiah says “The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself”, he did not ask anybody for permission. Nothing a preacher can do can stop it. He will fill Babylon the Great with men as with caterpillers, the terrorists and sleeper cells of the nations she robbed. Whether we are ready or not, the Most High is going to bring this to pass, so we do not need to be playing games.

To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house. It's all going back to Matthew 4:15-16 and Isaiah 9:1-2.
precepts.point: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. So Christ was that great light that was being spoken of.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles.” The one given for a light is Christ, the great light that sprung up in Galilee.

Those Gentiles there are not talking about other nations. It is talking about what we just read in Matthew: “Galilee of the Gentiles”, the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim, the tribes of Israel carried away and called Gentiles.

Why is he sent? “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” Them that sit in darkness are the same “people which sat in darkness” in Matthew 4:16, the people that walked in darkness in Isaiah 9. It all goes back to Matthew 4:15-16 and Isaiah 9:1-2.

So when Christ began to preach “Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand”, he was the covenant of the people and the light of the Gentiles, sent to Israel sitting in darkness to bring them out of the prison house.

precepts.text: All that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries go into captivity; every nation had a hand in spoiling us, the Arabs included, and what you see overseas is the Lord's righteous judgment.
precepts.point: For a prey and none delivereth, for a spoil and none saith restore: no nation speaks on our behalf unless a cheque is involved, and none will restore what it stole, from Henrietta Lacks' cells on down, because restoring us means giving back everything.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls Israel “a people robbed and spoiled.” We are robbed of our nationality, robbed of the understanding that we are the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. Jeremiah shows how we are spoiled, and what the Lord will do about it.

“Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured”: that is going to take place upon the oppressors of our people. “and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: the adversaries are all the nations outside of the children of Israel, and every one of the nations that oppress us shall go into captivity.

How do they spoil us? Over a multitude of captivities the children of Israel have gone into, every single nation has had its hand in the oppression of the twelve tribes. That includes the Arabs, that a lot of brothers and sisters want to cry over when they see what is going on in Palestine. Those people had our people oppressed too; they were spoiling the hell out of us. What we are seeing overseas right now is the righteous judgment of the Lord, prophecy fulfilling right now.

Yet brothers and sisters are so damn fearful to escape this captivity and get themselves together, even as the prophecies come to pass. Many are called, but few are chosen, so self-examine. With bombs dropping and rumors of war, men are still catting around, committing fornication, letting their wives rule over them and hide their folly, paying for prostitutes, hooked on marijuana and controlled by the porn system. Our people are sick; they are afraid of freedom, because sin controls them.

“and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.” The nations that spoiled us shall in turn be a spoil for us, because the tables are turned. We serve a just God. So Isaiah’s people “for a prey” and “for a spoil” will not stay that way: those that prey upon Israel are given for a prey themselves.

precepts.text: This is a people robbed and spoiled, and none saith, restore.
precepts.point: Their Redeemer is strong and will plead their cause and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together: and all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go.” A narrow-minded person thinks only of the fields, but look at the economic and resource oppression on the continents where we reside: both kingdoms, all twelve tribes, suffering the same afflictions. They hold us fast because of the resources in our lands.

Isaiah describes that same people: “But this is a people robbed and spoiled; they are all of them snared in holes, and they are hid in prison houses: they are for a prey, and none delivereth; for a spoil, and none saith, Restore.” Robbed and spoiled is the same as the oppression we read of in Micah.

Robbed goes to our identity, not only our resources. The thesaurus lays it out: cut off, deprived, destitute, dispossessed; and because we are not living as the sons of God, we accept what they call us, Gentiles, and become impoverished, without hope, without a redeemer, without access to our own resources, stripped. Spoiled, in the sense meant here, is being severely damaged or harmed in a way that reduces value: marred or ruined. We are the sons of God, the greatest people the Lord ever created, for whom he made the whole earth, and that is not what we reap now.

“none delivereth”, “none saith, Restore”: that is why our Redeemer must come and do it. “Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is his name”, and that Redeemer is Christ. Notice all the re- words with Israel: redeemed, restored, redemption. They show the covenant never passed on to some strangers or foreign nation. Our people have got to wake up.

precepts.text: He will magnify the law and make it honourable; Christ magnified the law, he did not do away with the sacrifice principle.
precepts.point: Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.” Christ magnified the law. He did not do away with it, and he did not do away with the sacrifice principle; he made it honourable.

So the curse on him “that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them” still stands for us. The sacrifice transformed from the animal to our own bodies, presented holy and acceptable unto God, but the law itself was magnified, not removed. If your sacrifice is not holy, the Son is not presenting you before the Father.

precepts.text: I am the Lord, that is my name, and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images. That is why no fire came for Baal.
precepts.point: From midday past the time of the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor any to answer nor any that regarded. No one answered because the Most High will not give his glory to another, and the gods of the nations are idols that are not real; they are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“I am the Lord: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.” That is why no fire came for Baal.

The prophets of Baal dressed their bullock and called on Baal “from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered.” Eight hundred and fifty men leaped upon the altar, running wild, while Elijah sat back watching the madness. At noon he mocked them: “Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.”

They cried aloud and “cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them”, for cutting themselves was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal. Still “there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.” The Most High will not give his glory to another.

precepts.text: The Most High gave Jacob for a spoil because they would not walk in His ways nor obey His law.
precepts.point: He sold His people for nothing and did not increase His wealth by their price.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy: and they which hate us spoil for themselves. Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen.” Isaiah asks who did it: “Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers? did not the Lord, he against whom we have sinned? for they would not walk in his ways, neither were they obedient unto his law.”

The enemy gained the power to spoil us because the Most High gave us over for our sins. He cast off, put us to shame and went not forth with our armies, not because the heathen were stronger, but because we would not walk in his ways nor obey his law.

precepts.text: I am the Lord, that is My name, and My glory will I not give to another; the graven images are the idols.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory”. The Most High says the same of himself: “I am the Lord: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.”

The graven images are the idols of the psalm, silver and gold, the work of men's hands. His glory goes to his name alone, not to another, and his praise is not for graven images.

note.label: Isaiah 42: My Servant and the Light of the Gentiles

precepts.why:
“Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.” This goes into Christ, and Matthew shows who the gentiles are: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.”

Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes, and their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles, the land and the region of the gentiles. So the gentiles the servant brings judgment to are the children of Israel, the people which sat in darkness and saw great light. He shall not fail nor be discouraged “till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law.”

precepts.point: A bruised reed he shall not break and the smoking flax he shall not quench; he shall bring forth judgment unto truth. He shall not fail nor be discouraged till he has set judgment in the earth, and the isles shall wait for his law.

note.label: Isaiah 42: My Servant and the Light of the Gentiles

precepts.why:
Right after Zebulun and Naphtali are called Galilee of the Gentiles, “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ began his preaching to those same tribes called gentiles.

That is the servant bringing forth “judgment to the Gentiles”: the spirit put upon him, preaching repent to the children of Israel in the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim. He did not cry nor lift up nor cause his voice to be heard in the street; he preached the kingdom of heaven to Israel, the gentiles of Isaiah 42.

precepts.text: Make no graven image to bow down and serve it, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God; it is not that images cannot be made, since angels stood in the temple, but that they must not be made to worship them.
precepts.point: They shall be turned back and greatly ashamed that trust in graven images, that say to the molten images, ye are our gods.

note.label: Isaiah 42: My Servant and the Light of the Gentiles

precepts.why:
“They shall be turned back, they shall be greatly ashamed, that trust in graven images, that say to the molten images, Ye are our gods.” That shame is for breaking the commandment: “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me. Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God”.

It is not that images cannot be made, since angels stood in the temple. It is that they must not be made to bow down to and serve them; make no graven image to worship it, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God, “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.”

The Most High has long held his peace, because all the prophecies in this bible must be fulfilled, and once that happens it is going down: he will cry like a travailing woman and destroy and devour at once. The blind he will bring by a way they knew not and not forsake them, but those that say to the molten images, ye are our gods, shall be turned back and greatly ashamed.

precepts.text: The prophecy quoted: mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; a bruised reed shall he not break.
precepts.point: This too was written beforehand: behold my servant, whom I have chosen, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

note.label: Matthew 12: Lord of the Sabbath and the Blasphemy Against the Holy Ghost

precepts.why:
The Pharisees held a council how they might destroy him, and he withdrew, healed the multitudes that followed, and “charged them that they should not make him known”. This too was written beforehand, and Matthew says so: “That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet”.

Isaiah: “Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.” The servant, the elect in whom the Lord's soul delights, with the spirit put upon him, is Christ, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

“He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street.” That is why he withdrew from the council and charged the people not to make him known: no crying in the streets. “A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.” The one the Pharisees wanted to destroy was quietly healing them all, breaking no bruised reed and quenching no smoking flax, exactly as it was written.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles”. The light shining on Israel again.

The thought continues in verse 7: “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” Them that sit in darkness are Isaiah 9:1-2, the northern kingdom, brought out of the prison house of captivity. So the Gentiles here are them that sit in darkness: the northern kingdom, not all nations, whatever your stupid commentaries say. Damn what Esau’s commentary says; we are the people of God, and it is our book, not theirs.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

precepts.why: “The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war”. “He shall prevail against his enemies.” “I have long time holden my peace”: I sat back quiet for centuries. “I have been still, and refrained myself”: refrained from intervening for the Israelites. “Now will I cry like a travailing woman”: I’m going to scream like a woman in childbirth pains. “I will destroy and devour at once”: he’s talking about the nations. “I will make waste mountains and hills”: governments and smaller governments.

note.label: The Getaway 3

precepts.why: “And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not”. “I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight”: hopefully that light is made straight in the dark path our brothers are walking down, and Christ is illuminated, and they come to understand Christ and the New Covenant and remove the veil from their face.

note.label: The Guide to Fixing a Broken People

precepts.why: What is sin? Somebody new could be looking on Facebook right now and not understand what sin is. “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” Sin is the breaking of God’s laws. This is what we must understand, and that’s what we did: “he against whom we have sinned” means we broke God’s laws, and he got angry.

note.label: The Guide to Fixing a Broken People

precepts.why:
Our people run into the gangs, they run into the church. “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”.

“And thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”: the Lord said we was not going to prosper in our ways, and he’s proven it to be true. We’re not prospering, we’re only declining.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed”: our oppressed people are broken people. “And spoiled evermore”: we spoiled, like spoiled rotten meat, like milk you can’t drink. The young women out in the projects here in Nashville with a song telling folks to come outside, all of them with them big ass eyelashes like caterpillars crawling across their face: they want you to come outside so they can fight, they want a brawl. This is happening because our people are broken; they don’t know how to love their neighbors, how to love themselves. “And no man shall save thee”.

note.label: The Acts Of The Apostles & Foundation Through Christ

precepts.why:
“He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.”

Matthew shows Christ fulfilling Isaiah 42. He did not come to argue in the streets with those trying to catch him in his words; he came with the Father’s doctrine, knowing why he was sent.

note.label: The Acts Of The Apostles & Foundation Through Christ

precepts.why:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim”. Didn’t we read about the land of Zebulun just a few moments ago, in the ninth chapter of Isaiah? When Christ came on the scene, he came and fulfilled exactly what was written of him.

“By the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Galilee of who? Of the Gentiles. The Bible is letting you know in the New Testament that the Gentiles are Israelites. Yes, the Gentiles are Israelites.

“The people which sat in darkness saw great light”. So the “light of the Gentiles” in Isaiah 42:6 is the light that shined on Zebulun and Naphtali: Israel.

note.label: The Acts Of The Apostles & Foundation Through Christ

precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives”. To the captives.

“And recovering of sight to the blind”: remember, Isaiah just said “To open the blind eyes”. “To set at liberty them that are bruised”: the bruised reed of Isaiah 42:3, “A bruised reed shall he not break”. He’s telling you exactly who he came for.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.”

points: “And give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles”. “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house”: through the spirit of Christ, that’s our job, to bring the true message of Christ to our brothers and sisters of the northern kingdom, the so-called Hispanics and natives, and of the southern kingdom, the so-called Negroes, even those who don’t believe in Christ, out of that darkness into the marvellous light.

note.label: The Getaway 3

points: These are well-known scriptures. “But this is a people robbed and spoiled”: the people that have been robbed and spoiled are the Israelites, us, our families.

“They are all of them snared in holes”: a snare is a trap, a catch, a bag net. We have been entrapped. What are these traps? Religion: the people jumping around on the TV screen talking about they got the Holy Ghost, the prosperity gospel preaching they put up on TikTok, looking like they saying some profound knowledge, and it’s stupid. Look at this nasty woman twerking at church: there’s a snare in the damn hole. It got her in the strip club spirit, throwing that ass in church. That’s why we tell y’all to come out the Christian church; we got to come out these Christian churches.

Look at these little boy monsters: these games and this rap music are snares in the hole. They hope one day to get rich, hope one day the Jewish man is gonna get them ten thousand dollars a piece so they get them a chain and be broke again. He ain’t got no haircut, his pants sagging, he ain’t got no sense to put no belt on, and they all smoking weed. This is a broken people. We got to stop this somewhere, man; we got to fix our broken people. This is why it’s important for us to hit the street and put boots on the ground, why it’s important for the editing team to keep pushing videos out on social media: the Lord is using you to push this truth.

“And they are hid in prison houses”: our people are hid in prison houses. How do we fix this? “They are for a prey, and none delivereth”: they fall prey. Who are the hunters? Right now the so-called government, the white man, even our own people as we’ve seen them in Memphis. The wicked are the hunters and we the prey. You can’t even put no color on it no more; the scripture says it’s the wicked, and the wicked gonna be his sword.

“For a spoil, and none saith, Restore”: nobody’s saying restore these people. Nobody’s saying let’s get to the root of the problem: how did they end up over here, who brought them over here, and why did he do it? It’s like looking at a tree: you’re looking at the bad fruit on the tree, but not at why the fruit ended up dying on the tree like that, whether the soil is bad, the roots, the seed. You’re just looking at the fruit, and the fruit is Christianity, politics, all these things we’re trying to use to fix our problems.

note.label: The Guide to Fixing a Broken People

This is the guide to fixing our problems: we got to first understand God put us in this situation, because we disobeyed him, so we put ourselves in this situation. People say we always blaming the white man. We don’t blame the white man; we just saying the white man is the Lord’s sword, carrying out certain things, and we use the white man or the government or anybody else to show that our people are in these conditions. These are the people carrying out God’s plan and his judgments upon us.
“He against whom we have sinned”: it’s telling you what happened. We sinned against God; we broke God’s laws, statutes and his commandments. We pissed God off, we broke his law, he got mad.

“For they would not walk in his ways”: we want to do our own thing. We’ve been a disobedient people; just like now we complain, but we would not do what God commands us to do. They say get that Bible out of here, we don’t want them here. “Neither were they obedient unto his law”: just like today our people do not want to keep God’s laws. It’s the Lord’s Sabbath day, but we don’t want to remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy. note.label: The Guide to Fixing a Broken People

note.label: The Acts Of The Apostles & Foundation Through Christ

points: “A bruised reed shall he not break”. That is referring to the northern kingdom. “And the smoking flax shall he not quench”: he’s not going to quench their spirit.

points: “He shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law.”

points: “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” From the prisons, the shadow of death. That is who the light of the Gentiles comes for.

points: “He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street.” Christ was not argumentative: he said what he said and walked off. That’s why when we teach something, that’s it; we’re not debating with nobody. What the Bible says is what it is.
